requirements.title: Formatted records are representable character sequences
requirements.definition: A formatted record consists of a sequence of characters representable in the processor.

pending.formatted-record-character-sequence: Use future formatted internal WRITE to a CHARACTER variable prefilled with a nonblank sentinel and expect exact representable characters, then formatted READ them back into a sentinel buffer.

requirements.title: Processors may prohibit some control characters in formatted records
requirements.definition: A processor may prohibit some control characters from appearing in a formatted record.

pending.formatted-control-character-prohibition-: No portable oracle exists for which control characters, if any, are prohibited; future tests must not require acceptance or rejection of a particular control character except where another rule fixes it.

requirements.title: Formatted record length is measured in characters and primarily depends on written characters
requirements.definition: The length of a formatted record is measured in characters and depends primarily on the number of characters put into the record when it is written.

pending.formatted-length-measured-in-characters: Use an internal formatted WRITE of a known three-character record and assert exact three-character content; external maximum or storage representation is not asserted.

requirements.title: Formatted records are read or written only by formatted input/output statements
requirements.definition: Formatted records shall be read or written only by formatted input/output statements.

pending.formatted-records-formatted-io-only: Positive plan reads and writes a known formatted record with formatted I/O. A negative source-control may attempt unformatted I/O on that formatted connection, but no diagnostic facet is filed unless a future rule provides a portable required rejection.

requirements.title: Formatted record length has processor/media latitude and may be zero
requirements.definition: Formatted record length may depend on the processor and external medium, and may be zero.

pending.formatted-length-processor-or-medium-dep: No portable oracle may assert an external formatted record length when the processor or medium can affect it; future tests use internal records for exact character counts.
pending.formatted-zero-length-record-permitted: Future test writes an empty formatted record only where record positioning rules are registered; anti-vacuity requires surrounding nonempty records so the empty record position is observable.
